declared_purpose: Agent-first web/news search, docs/code lookup, company research, extraction, crawling, mapping, and structured evidence packs with explainable routing. Node is required; premium credentials are optional and a no-key baseline is promised. Federation, caching, health persistence, provider ranking, and automatic research expansion are implementation choices supporting that purpose, not requirements for every retrieval (SKILL.md:1-23; scripts/lib/config.mjs:441-483).

data_operations.operation: Read local configuration and runtime inputs
data_operations.source: CLI arguments, working directory, optional config.json or WEB_SEARCH_PRO_CONFIG, and environment variables
data_operations.data_scope: Queries, URLs, filters, budgets, provider configuration, credential availability, and selected adapters' API credentials.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Node process; configuration reads alone do not disclose these remotely.
data_operations.condition: On command execution. Defaults are merged with file configuration, environment settings, and command overrides.

data_operations.data_scope: Query augmented with requested domain operators; fixed browser and language headers. Receives HTML and parses bounded result snippets.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/
data_operations.condition: When ddg executes on a cache miss. Tries a curl POST; a thrown error triggers a fetch GET containing the query in the URL.

data_operations.operation: Send Tavily search or extraction requests
data_operations.data_scope: Search: query, count, depth, news/date/domain filters, and TAVILY_API_KEY; requests an answer without raw search content. Extract: supplied URLs and the API credential; receives extracted content and failures.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Search: https://api.tavily.com/search; extraction: https://api.tavily.com/extract
data_operations.condition: When the credentialed adapter executes as the selected provider, search fanout, or eligible extraction fallback.

data_operations.operation: Send Exa search or extraction requests
data_operations.data_scope: Search: query, count, search mode, domain/date filters, automatic prompting, and highlights request. Extraction: supplied URL IDs, full-text request, and livecrawl fallback. EXA_API_KEY authenticates both.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Search: https://api.exa.ai/search; extraction: https://api.exa.ai/contents
data_operations.condition: When the credentialed adapter executes as selected search, fanout, or extraction provider/fallback.

data_operations.data_scope: Query, count, supplied language/country/domain/time filters, and QUERIT_API_KEY as bearer authentication.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Endpoint resolved from QUERIT_BASE_URL and QUERIT_BASE_PATH; defaults to https://api.querit.ai/v1/search.
data_operations.condition: When Querit executes. The base URL is safety-checked before endpoint construction; an override determines the actual resolved recipient.

data_operations.data_scope: Query with domain operators, result count, date/time filters, supplied country/language, and SERPER_API_KEY in a header.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://google.serper.dev/search or https://google.serper.dev/news
data_operations.condition: When Serper executes; the news option selects the endpoint.

data_operations.data_scope: Query, result count, extra-snippet request, supplied country/language and freshness filters in the URL; BRAVE_API_KEY in the subscription header.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search
data_operations.condition: When Brave executes.

data_operations.data_scope: SERPAPI_API_KEY, query, selected sub-engine, count, and applicable date/news/locale filters in URL parameters.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://serpapi.com/search.json
data_operations.condition: When SerpAPI executes. Google-specific date and news parameters depend on the selected sub-engine.

data_operations.data_scope: Query, count, fixed safesearch setting, supplied country/language and freshness in URL parameters; YOU_API_KEY in a header.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://ydc-index.io/v1/search
data_operations.condition: When You.com executes; returned web/news groups are selected and bounded locally.

data_operations.data_scope: Query with domain operators, news/time settings, and configured SEARXNG_LANGUAGE, SEARXNG_ENGINES, and safesearch settings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The configured SEARXNG_INSTANCE_URL followed by /search.
data_operations.condition: When the configured adapter executes, following a safety check of the instance URL. Results are limited locally.

data_operations.data_scope: Query, fixed system prompt, model selection, and bearer credential. Native transport adds supported domain/date/language filters; gateway transport incorporates domain operators and supplied constraints into the user prompt. Retrieved research evidence is not included in this request body.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Custom PERPLEXITY_BASE_URL gateway first; otherwise https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/sonar, OpenRouter's default or OPENROUTER_BASE_URL endpoint, or https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway/chat/completions.
data_operations.condition: First complete credential path wins: custom gateway, native, OpenRouter, then Kilo. Executes only when this adapter is called.

data_operations.operation: Pass HTTP request material to a local transport
data_operations.data_scope: Request URL, headers, and optional body; these can contain search data and adapter credentials. Responses are buffered as text.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local curl subprocess arguments when curl is used; otherwise built-in fetch. This is a local process boundary in addition to the remote request.
data_operations.condition: Shared-client adapters and Safe Fetch use curl when available unless a transport is explicitly selected.

data_operations.data_scope: Hostname resolution, target URL path/query, fixed user-agent and accept headers; response body, title, readable text, and links. maxChars truncates extracted content after retrieval.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured system DNS resolution for non-IP hostnames; requested page hosts and redirect destinations; response data enters local memory.
data_operations.condition: Direct-fetch extraction and crawl/map visits. Rejects unsupported schemes, URL userinfo, specified local/private targets, and rechecks each redirect. No page JavaScript is executed by this path.

data_operations.data_scope: Entry URLs, discovered links, page titles/content, traversal depth, parent URLs, failures, and optional robots.txt rules. Mapping returns nodes and edges rather than page content.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Visited page hosts; optional /robots.txt hosts; local traversal memory and the command caller.
data_operations.condition: On crawl/map cache misses, within depth/page limits. Discovery defaults to entry origins; cross-origin discovery requires an override. Path filters apply to discovered pages. Robots retrieval is optional and disabled by default.

data_operations.operation: Infer routing signals and optionally disclose a query to multiple providers
data_operations.source: Search signal analysis, routing confidence, and federated search
data_operations.data_scope: Locally inferred query intent, freshness/privacy/multilingual signals, provider scores and confidence. Execution sends the query and applicable filters to each planned provider; results are reranked and deduplicated locally.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local planner and caller; selected provider plus configured fanout providers only when federation triggers.
data_operations.condition: Federation is disabled by default. When enabled, matching triggers can add providers; explicit --engine or primary-only merging disables fanout. A successful primary response does not cancel planned fanout.

data_operations.operation: Retry unresolved extraction URLs with eligible fallback providers
data_operations.data_scope: Initially all supplied URLs; subsequently only URLs lacking nonempty extracted content. Successful results and failures are merged locally.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected extraction adapter and remaining eligible extraction adapters, with their respective remote or direct-fetch recipients.
data_operations.condition: Automatic extraction continues while URLs remain unresolved. An explicit engine restricts the candidate set; successful URLs are removed from subsequent attempts.

data_operations.operation: Expand a research request into retrieval tasks
data_operations.data_scope: Topic-derived search queries and domain constraints; first seed URL for extraction and mapping; optional dossier crawl. Local evidence gaps can generate up to two follow-up tasks.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Providers and target hosts used by the search/extract/map/crawl primitives; local orchestration state.
data_operations.condition: Research execution outside --plan. Task budgets constrain expansion; a seed URL automatically adds a map task. CLI --no-federation disables fanout, and CLI research disables rendering.

data_operations.operation: Derive research attributes and evidence summaries
data_operations.source: Research classification, evidence normalization, and findings components
data_operations.data_scope: Topic type/signals, research axes, cleaned text, claims, source authority/credibility, freshness, coverage, quality, conflicts, and confidence. These are heuristic attributes of requests and sources, not verified personal traits.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local analysis and the returned research pack.
data_operations.condition: Planning derives topic attributes; executed retrievals produce evidence attributes and findings. Noise filtering removes entries from the assembled evidence, not from previously written primitive caches.

data_operations.source: Cache component and command/research call sites
data_operations.data_scope: SHA-256 keys derived from queries/URLs and options; JSON payloads containing search queries, answers, results, extracted content, crawl pages, map graphs, failures, and routing summaries, plus timestamps.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured cache directory, default .cache/web-search-pro, in search/extract/crawl/map subdirectories. Hashed filenames do not anonymize plaintext payloads.
data_operations.condition: Caching is enabled by default. Valid hits return stored results without executing retrieval. Misses write payloads; default TTL is 1,800 seconds for search and 21,600 seconds for extraction/crawl/map.

data_operations.data_scope: Provider identifier, failure counts, cooldown, success/failure timestamps, raw last error message, and inferred error category/status.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: .cache/web-search-pro/health-state.json by default, independently of retrieval-cache enablement.
data_operations.condition: Health tracking is enabled by default. Search/extraction outcomes update it; success clears lastError and cooldown but preserves the prior failure timestamp.

data_operations.operation: Return plans, retrieval results, and diagnostics to the caller
data_operations.data_scope: Requested results, query/topic, evidence, route explanations, configured-provider names, credential-presence indicators, configuration/path information, cache statistics, and health/errors as applicable.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Command stdout/stderr and its caller. These returns alone do not establish an additional remote disclosure.
data_operations.condition: JSON or Markdown output. Search/extract/research --plan skips retrieval. Doctor/bootstrap/review inspect configuration and stored state; bootstrap's sample queries are route plans, not live searches.

data_operations.data_scope: Expired entry being read, or JSON entries in the four retrieval-cache subdirectories.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local cache filesystem; health-state.json is outside the clear operation's enumerated subdirectories.
data_operations.condition: Expired records are removed when that exact key is read. Explicit cache clear removes enumerated entries. Cache stats counts files without pruning them.

potential_excess.data_scope: URL username/password fields, if present in extraction inputs.
potential_excess.condition: A premium extraction adapter receives credential-bearing URLs. Both serialize supplied URLs without the direct-fetch userinfo check.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Public URL extraction needs target URLs; the documented Safe Fetch boundary explicitly rejects credential-bearing URLs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Submit permitted public URLs to the selected extraction provider.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reject credential-bearing URLs before any extraction-provider submission. This removes extra credential data from a required request rather than removing extraction itself.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep accepted public URLs and semantically necessary query parameters intact; preserve existing rejection behavior for unsafe inputs.

potential_excess.data_scope: Raw provider failure text, including response bodies and any request data those bodies echo.
potential_excess.condition: Health tracking records a failed search/extraction. lastError persists until replaced or cleared by a later success; no age-based removal is implemented.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Routing health requires failure classification, counters, timestamps, and cooldown; complete provider response bodies are an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain enough structured information to classify failures and enforce cooldown.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Persist status/category and a bounded, redacted diagnostic code instead of raw error text.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve classification before discarding raw text and retain the counters/timestamps used by routing.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired cached queries, URLs, answers, page content, graphs, failures, and routing metadata.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: search/extract/crawl/map JSON files beneath the configured cache directory.
potential_excess.condition: A cached key expires but is never read again and cache clear is not invoked. TTL prevents reuse but does not itself delete the file.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared cache contract includes TTL telemetry; expired payloads no longer supply valid cache hits.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep reusable payloads during their configured validity period.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Prune expired files during bounded maintenance or cache operations, rather than relying solely on rereading the same key.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain unexpired entries and existing cache-hit behavior; avoid extending retention while pruning.

potential_excess.data_scope: Extracted text beyond the requested maxChars, notably research's 4,000-character extraction budget.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local extraction result, extraction-cache JSON, and caller/research evidence pack.
potential_excess.condition: Tavily/Exa extraction ignores the passed options. Research also plans with task.options.maxChars but executes with context.config, whose default fetch limit is 12,000.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The CLI explicitly offers a per-URL text limit, and research tasks explicitly budget 4,000 characters.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Extract readable content within the requested per-URL limit.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Apply the task limit during execution and enforce it on all adapter results before output or caching. Narrow provider-side retrieval only where its supported API is established.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep URL/title/type and failure metadata. Server-side extraction limits are unresolved; local trimming alone does not reduce the already received provider response.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated seed-page URLs and overlapping page-response bodies.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The same seed/discovered page hosts, and repeated local response buffers.
potential_excess.condition: Research with a seed URL schedules mapping and, for an allowed dossier crawl, crawling independently. On cache misses, overlapping pages are fetched separately; direct-fetch extraction can repeat the seed request again.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Research needs readable evidence and site structure, but separate network fetches of the same current page are not themselves required outcomes.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Produce extraction, map, and crawl projections with their respective depth, page, and text limits.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse compatible request-scoped fetched snapshots across these primitives. This removes redundant retrieval actions, not fields from an otherwise necessary request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve freshness and safety validation, complete map coverage, crawl content limits, and differing provider semantics; do not substitute a short map text projection for a longer crawl result.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local HTTP transport buffers and Node response memory.
potential_excess.condition: Safe Fetch requests a URL returning an unsupported content type. The shared transport reads the response body before fetchUrlSnapshot checks the content type.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared boundary blocks unsupported binary downloads; these bodies are not usable by the static text retrieval outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Request the target and identify whether its response is supported.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Inspect response headers and abort unsupported bodies before buffering them. This narrows data received in the required GET rather than adding a separate probe request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve redirect checks and supported HTML/text retrieval; retain an appropriate unsupported-type failure.

potential_excess.data_scope: Provider results exceeding the caller's requested count.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Selected search provider's response and local normalization/reranking memory.
potential_excess.condition: Requested count is below routing.maxPerProvider. Even without triggered federation, the primary request uses the larger count, then final results are sliced to the requested count.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Returning the requested count is explicit; maintaining a larger reranking pool is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve enough results to satisfy the requested count.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the requested count for a single-provider path unless a larger ranking pool is explicitly needed; make overfetch a separate bounded policy.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain deliberate overfetch when the required ranking/diversity outcome depends on it. This reduces response data in a required request, not the number of provider calls.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second copy of crawl page content and associated page fields.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Crawl-cache JSON payload, where both results and pages contain the page records.
potential_excess.condition: A crawl payload is cached, including research crawl tasks.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The caller may require the existing output schema, but two persisted copies are unnecessary to reconstruct it.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain one complete crawl representation and reproduce the required output fields.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Store one canonical page collection internally and reconstruct results/pages when returning the payload.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the caller-visible schema, page content, ordering, and cache semantics.

unknowns: Actual invocations, environment values, and optional configuration were not supplied; active providers, concrete overridden recipients, and runtime data contents remain conditional.
Provider retention, logging, training, downstream forwarding, and remote extraction behavior are undocumented here. SearXNG's privacy label does not establish its configured instance's behavior.
Whether premium extraction APIs support server-side content limits is unresolved; their remote crawling, target access, and JavaScript behavior cannot be inferred from local Safe Fetch.
Operating-system logging, curl configuration/proxies, and caller retention or onward transmission of stdout are outside the supplied source.
No source-coverage blocker remains. The audit establishes packaged behavior and conditional minimization opportunities, not observed execution or external deletion guarantees.
